chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not permissible for a menstruating woman to take a qusrah or a jummah.'

key_terms.جُمَّةً: A specific hairstyle or hair arrangement (jummah)
key_terms.حَاضَتْ: Menstruating (woman in the state of hayd)
key_terms.قُصَّةً: A specific hairstyle or hair arrangement (kusrah)

ai.seo_question: What hairstyle is prohibited for menstruating women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes a specific legal ruling (hukm) prohibiting menstruating women from wearing 'qusrah' or 'jummah,' traditional elaborate hairstyles often associated with adornment and social display. While some scholars interpret this as a restriction on excessive beautification during the state of ritual impurity (hayd), others view it as a recommendation (mustahabb) to maintain modesty and simplicity, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on aligning physical appearance with spiritual state.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not Permissible for the menstruating woman that she takes (a hairstyle of) hair upon the forehead or form knots’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Misma’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
has said, ‘It is not lawful for a woman during her experiencing Hayd (menses) to form her hairs in a knot or allow a portion to hang down her forehead.’”
